title: ADAPTIVE GENERATION OF BIAS-ELICITING QUESTIONS FOR LLMS
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, named CAB (Counterfactual Assessment of Bias), measures unwanted, implicit bias against different religious groups. It uses realistic, open-ended questions designed to elicit differential treatment in everyday scenarios that are not explicitly about religion. Specific bias categories evaluated include Stereotyped Profession/Interest Linkage, Faith-Framed Language & Value Attribution, Unrequested Identity Insertion, Practice/Observance Assumptions, and Disparate Neutrality vs. Accommodation Guidance.
findings: Biases related to religion were found to be more subtle compared to other attributes like sex. The majority of biased behaviors involved models including unwanted faith-related terms in their answers or linking specific religions to certain preferences (e.g., a Christian being more measure-oriented, while Muslims and Hindus were more locally value-oriented). A key challenge noted was generating questions that elicit unwanted bias without touching on legitimate differences like dietary restrictions or workdays, which led the authors to explicitly instruct their generation model to avoid such topics.
references: Ajwad Abrar, Nafisa Tabassum Oeshy, Mohsinul Kabir, and Sophia Ananiadou. Religious bias landscape in language and text-to-image models: Analysis, detection, and debiasing strategies. ArXiv preprint, abs/2501.08441, 2025. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.08441.
